clue.text: Show stress on island

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or stress them

explanation.surface: Someone puts the pressure on while performing on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi was a long-running American television sitcom, so it is an example of a show.

clue.text: See 5
State shark attack? It's part of the memory

indicators.note: to state something is to say it out loud, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: what a shark does when it attacks is bite

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a shark attack, then a remark that it is something remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' signals that we hear the word for a shark attack, which sounds like the computing term.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer's memory is measured in units of eight bits, each such unit being a small part of storage.

clue.text: Cruise for one mile, say, like sailor

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated EG
as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor goes on a mile-long cruise in nautical fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' looks like a sea voyage but is Tom Cruise, the film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Cruise is a hugely famous film actor, an example of a celebrity of the highest rank.

clue.text: Robert Shaw performing — grandeur oddly missing inside film studio

indicators.note: the remaining letters go within the rearranged name
performing suggests the letters of the actor's name are put to work in a new order
the odd-placed letters of grandeur are dropped, leaving only the even ones

explanation.surface: Robert Shaw, the Jaws actor, acting at a film studio without any grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Shaw played Quint in Jaws. 'performing' signals the rearrangement of his name; 'oddly missing' keeps the even letters of grandeur, and 'inside' places them within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Warner Brothers is a major Hollywood production company, so it is an example of a film studio.

clue.text: It's blown up in the sea — fiction about fine sailor on Spielberg film

definitions.text: It's blown up in the sea

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for fiction surrounds the letter for fine

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a generic name for a sailor
E.T. is the 1982 Steven Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A tale of a sailor in a Spielberg film, set at sea with something exploding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown up' suggests an explosion, as at the end of Jaws, but means inflated.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable buoyancy vest is inflated to keep a wearer afloat in the water.

clue.text: Most biting great white shark, initially not good when swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about freely, so they are rearranged
not means without, so the letter for good is dropped
initially means take the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: The fiercest great white shark is not a good thing to meet when swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' takes G out of great, giving REAT; 'initially' adds W and S; 'swimming' rearranges REATWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw wind is bitingly cold, so the superlative means the most bitter or biting.

clue.text: Group drink

definitions.meaning: a group, especially of birds or women
informal British slang for an alcoholic drink, short for beverage

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flock or company and, in British slang, a drink.

clue.text: Display 26 across fish

parts.note: the answer to 26 across is a noble gas whose chemical symbol is Ar
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: An aquarium showing off a fish from another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an impressive display or arrangement of things.

clue.text: Destroy one caught — time to see catch

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the word for seeing holds or catches the pieces inside it

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught and destroyed, with a time arranged to see the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' is the containment signal: DATE catches IC to make DICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or root out completely, a synonym for destroying.

clue.text: Primarily at sea

definitions.meaning: the main is an old word for the open ocean, so this means out on the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for mostly, and literally places something on the ocean (the main).

clue.text: Time unknown — crew returning to east

indicators.note: returning means the word for crew is read backwards

parts.note: a crew is a group of men
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A ship's crew heads back east at an unknown time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is the definition, from the saying that time is the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is often called an adversary, as in the phrase 'time is the enemy'.

clue.text: See 18
Small crowd go away

parts.note: to cram is to crowd or pack tightly

explanation.surface: A small crowd is told to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal imperative telling someone to leave at once.

clue.text: Sailors turn on way and head for folly

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, i.e. sailors
U as in a U-turn
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Sailors set off down a road, making for a headland, which is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Folly is foolishness or ridiculousness, the quality of being nonsensical.

clue.text: Second note by Roy Scheider, say — one who responds

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Roy Scheider, who played Chief Brody in Jaws, is an example of an actor

explanation.surface: A second note from Roy Scheider, the Jaws star, replying to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reacts to a stimulus responds to it, so the noun names a responder.

clue.text: Introduction to Shark, found in upended box files

indicators.note: found in means the first letter sits inside the word for box
upended in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: introduction to means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sharky reference introduced into box files that have been turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts S inside SPAR to make SPSAR; 'upended' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps are coarse files used to shape wood or metal, so the plural noun is a type of file.

clue.text: Dangers rule lives — case of shark making comeback

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: making a comeback means the letters go backwards
the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: A warning that dangers live on as the shark returns, as in a sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes SK from shark; 'making comeback' turns it to KS.
explanation.definitionFit: Risks are hazards or chances of harm, plural nouns meaning dangers.

clue.text: Faces Chief Brody's unlimited time in rough waters

indicators.note: unlimited means losing its limits, the first and last letters
in means the letter for time goes inside the rearranged letters
rough describes choppy water, signalling the letters are churned

explanation.surface: Chief Brody of Jaws faces endless time in rough waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faces' is the band, not a verb. 'rough' turns waters to SEWAR; 'in' puts T inside, giving STEWART.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Stewart was lead singer of the Faces, the British rock band, so he was its leader.

clue.text: Dr No book (novel) — with a twist, it offers an escape

definitions.text: with a twist, it offers an escape

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A James Bond novel where a twist provides a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a description of the book but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning the handle on a door opens it, letting someone leave a room.

clue.text: Shark ultimately swallows one that worked with lines

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter

parts.note: to swallow is to eat, so swallows means eats

explanation.surface: A shark swallowing a man who worked on fishing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' suggests fishing, but means lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was a Romantic poet, whose work was writing lines of verse.

clue.text: In character of bad one at sea? Sound at start of horror

parts.note: as means in the role of, as an actor plays a part
a pirate is a villain on the sea

explanation.surface: An actor playing a villain at sea makes a noise as the horror film begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horror' looks like a film genre but the definition points to the breathy H sound at the start of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the breathy H sound, which begins the word horror when spoken.

clue.text: Opening sequence of movie (Jaws): ocean killer eats leading character from Amity Island

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so one piece swallows another
the opening letters of each word in sequence are taken
the leading character of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an orca is the killer whale, the ocean's top predator

explanation.surface: The opening of Jaws, where a killer of the sea feasts on a victim on Amity Island.
explanation.walkthrough: MJ swallows A to make MAJ. Amity Island is the fictional resort in Jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Picture cut up — Spielberg ultimately is outside during film cut

indicators.note: during means the inner group goes within the shortened film name
cut means the film's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Jaws is the 1975 Spielberg shark film

indicators.note: outside means the word is wraps around the letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter

explanation.surface: A director's cut of a Spielberg film, with a picture chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' appears twice: once in the definition (a picture cut up) and once telling us to trim the film's last letter. 'outside' and 'during' are the two containment signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw puzzle is a picture cut into interlocking pieces.

clue.text: Join American dad, heartlessly getting wind up

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: pop is an American name for a father
to wind up is to end

explanation.surface: An American father, unfeelingly, upsetting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach or add something on, a synonym for joining.

clue.text: Sea being cold, to work harbours

indicators.note: harbours means holds inside, so the word for work contains the other pieces

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written

explanation.surface: The sea is cold, so work goes on in harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea being' reads as a phrase about the sea but is the definition: a creature of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-armed mollusc is a marine creature, a being that lives in the sea.

clue.text: Note: at stern of legendary vessel is gas

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the letter goes at the end of the vessel

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A note pinned to the stern of a mythical ship is just hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas, element 18.

clue.text: Conservationists seeing that about social creatures

indicators.note: about means around, so the conjunction wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: as means because or seeing that
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservationists noticing something about animals that live in groups.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects that live in colonies, as these do, are classed as social creatures.

clue.text: Diving position to settle swimmer

parts.note: the pike is a diving position with straight legs and the body bent at the hips
to perch is to settle or alight

explanation.surface: A diver getting into position before settling down for a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikeperch, such as the zander, is a freshwater fish, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Ship's opening close to Matt Hooper struggling with line

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown about and rearranged
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The ship begins to close in on Matt Hooper, the shark expert in Jaws, who fights a fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like a start, but is a window in the side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A round window in a ship's hull is an opening in the vessel's side.

clue.text: See 28
Re station at sea, attacks physically

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A note regarding a station out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to assault someone violently, a vigorous physical attack.

clue.text: Measure length of animal

parts.note: to rate is to measure or assess

explanation.surface: Instructions to measure the length of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratel is the honey badger, an African and Asian mammal.
